summary: Fresh CLI 0.4.0 publisher (Delivery #1124) passed independent source review and 32+ synthetic controls, yet against the actual repository and services it had seven runtime defects found only by live reads: (1) the ordinary ledger App id/key/installation exist only as execution-pair-forward environment values, so a job without that environment mints with empty inputs; (2) ADR-0097 coverage needs the exact pinned-script lock step immediately after checkout in every credential-minting job; (3) frozen whole-file pins on a shared publisher workflow (0.3.0/0.3.1 controls) break when another route is appended; (4) a 120 s visibility window cannot cover nuget.org validation/signing; (5) GET rulesets/{id} omits the default update parameter and carries viewer metadata, so raw-response equality or hashing refuses; (6) GET releases/tags/{tag} 404s for drafts, requiring the authenticated release list; (7) dotnet nuget verify --all prints the repository service index only at -v normal. A separate gap remains: the public-load stage hides subprocess stderr (prints only the exception type and retains no artifact), so original run 42399710679 public-load CalledProcessError has no recoverable cause; a later local re-execution passed and stale flat-container/registration views after a fresh push are the unproven probable cause. Because the B publisher files are bound into the journal content identity, they cannot be edited for diagnostics or control changes during an original-forward recovery; such controls must be designed before the first send. Practice: before an irreversible route ships, exercise each native response and verifier against measured live shapes (not invented fixture text), pre-check finalization dependencies before the first send, retain bounded secret-free stderr for every effect-adjacent subprocess, and hold the producer main stable from enabling merge through finalization. This record grants no publication or forward authority.
title: Release-route controls must use measured live shapes; fixtures hid seven publisher defects
